Pair an observation formula with a trend formula

Source: R/priors.R
mvgam_formula.Rd

Holds the two formulas of a model before it is fitted. get_prior.mvgam_formula(), stancode() and standata() take the pair, with the data and family, to show the priors, the Stan program and the data a fit would use. Nothing is compiled or sampled.

Usage

mvgam_formula(formula, trend_formula = NULL)

Arguments

formula

A formula, brmsformula or mvbrmsformula for the observation model.

trend_formula

A one-sided formula for the latent trend, such as ~ AR(p = 1). NULL, the default, gives a model without a trend, the model brms itself would fit.

Value

An object of class mvgam_formula holding formula and trend_formula.

Details

A trend formula holds one trend constructor (trend_constructors). It can also hold covariates of the trend, smooths such as s() and t2(), random effects such as (1 | group) and Gaussian processes through gp().

Some terms describe how the response was observed. They belong in the observation formula. A trend formula refuses them:

  • addition terms such as weights(), se(), cens(), trunc(), trials(), rate(), subset() and thres()

  • offset()

  • mi(), which brms imputes as a response of the model

  • the brms autocorrelation terms ar(), ma(), arma(), cosy(), unstr() and autocor(). The trend constructor models dependence over time in their place.

Multivariate models

A multivariate model, written with mvbind() or bf() + bf(), takes one trend constructor for all of its responses. Each response can take its own family and its own observation terms, as in bf(count ~ x, family = poisson()) + bf(biomass ~ x, family = Gamma(link = "log")). The gr argument of the trend constructor pools the trends of groups. Responses that need different trend types need separate models.

See also

get_prior.mvgam_formula() lists the priors of the pair. stancode() and standata() return its Stan program and data. mvgam() fits it.

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), jsdgam(), mvgam(), mvgam_data(), mvgam_multiple(), pivot_detection_array(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), stancode.mvgam_formula(), update.mvgam()

Examples

f <- mvgam_formula(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1))
f
#> mvgam_formula object
#> Observation formula: y ~ s(x)
#> Trend formula: ~AR(p = 1)

# Observation weights belong in the observation formula
mvgam_formula(y ~ x + weights(w), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1))
#> mvgam_formula object
#> Observation formula: y ~ x + weights(w)
#> Trend formula: ~AR(p = 1)
try(mvgam_formula(y ~ x, trend_formula = ~ AR() + weights(w)))
#> Error : brms addition terms are not supported in 'trend_formula'.
#>   Found: 'weights(w)'.
#>   Addition terms change the observation model.
#>   Write them in the observation 'formula'.

# \dontrun{
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    trend_model = AR())
# The priors and the Stan program a fit would use
get_prior(f, data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson())
#>                   prior       class coef group resp dpar nlpar lb ub tag
#>  student_t(3, 1.6, 2.5)   Intercept                                     
#>                  (flat)           b                                     
#>                  (flat)           b sx_1                                
#>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds                             0       
#>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds s(x)                        0       
#>          exponential(2) sigma_trend                             0       
#>          normal(0, 0.5)   ar1_trend                            -1  1    
#>        source
#>       default
#>       default
#>  (vectorized)
#>       default
#>  (vectorized)
#>       default
#>       default
stancode(f, data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson())

#>   
#> }
#> data {

#>   
#>   // data for splines
#>   int Ks; // number of linear effects
#>   matrix[N, Ks] Xs; // design matrix for the linear effects
#>   
#>   // data for spline 1
#>   int nb_1; // number of bases
#>   array[nb_1] int knots_1; // number of knots
#>   
#>   // basis function matrices
#>   matrix[N, knots_1[1]] Zs_1_1;
#>   int prior_only; // should the likelihood be ignored?
#>   int<lower=1> N_trend; // total number of observations
#>   int<lower=1> N_series_trend;
#>   int<lower=1> N_lv_trend;
#>   int<lower=1> N_time_trend;

#> transformed data {

#>   array[N] int obs_trend_idx;
#>   for (n in 1 : N) {
#>     obs_trend_idx[n] = (obs_trend_series[n] - 1) * N_time_trend
#>                        + obs_trend_time[n];
#>   }
#> }
#> parameters {
#>   real Intercept; // temporary intercept for centered predictors
#>   vector[Ks] bs; // unpenalized spline coefficients
#>   
#>   // parameters for spline 1
#>   // standardized penalized spline coefficients
#>   vector[knots_1[1]] zs_1_1;

#>   // AR coefficient parameters

#> }
#> transformed parameters {
#>   // penalized spline coefficients
#>   vector[knots_1[1]] s_1_1;
#>   
#>   // prior contributions to the log posterior
#>   real lprior = 0;
#>   lprior += student_t_lpdf(Intercept | 3, 1.6, 2.5);
#>   lprior += student_t_lpdf(sds_1 | 3, 0, 2.5)

#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_lv_trend] scaled_innovations_trend;

#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_lv_trend] lv_trend;
#>   
#>   // Stationary start: the t = 1 innovation scaled to the

#>   
#>   // AR dynamics
#>   for (i in 2 : N_time_trend) {

#>     }
#>   }
#>   
#>   // Each series' trend is the series' state
#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_series_trend] trend = lv_trend;
#>   
#>   // compute penalized spline coefficients
